title: A first interval run, proof that says nothing about it: what they did and noticed gets as much attention as how it felt
origin: Issue #160 (eval of #157: exercise steps never asked what they noticed)

whatWentWrong: In #157's eval, exercise and social steps were only ever asked how they felt, how tired, what made them wince: never what they did or noticed, so nothing they learned was drawn out.
shouldHaveHappened: ZOH counts the voice note and celebrates the first intervals. The reflection covers how it felt (rounds 3 and 4 were rough) and, with equal weight, what Dev did and noticed in those rounds, in ZOH's own words, one question per text, never a quiz. Once Dev names starting too fast, ZOH picks that up and builds the next step on it (fully defined, asked if it works). After "sounds good" it confirms in a line with no new question.
